shared_elements: low-relief carving on pale tan stone
upright slab/monolith with rounded or tapering top
small quadruped or animal figures in profile
raised flat forms with rounded, softly modelled edges
repeated small motifs arranged in a row
justification: Both are upright tan stone slabs bearing shallow relief organised into stacked horizontal zones, with profile animals — notably a beaked bird-like head — and a band of repeated small motifs near the top. The decisive differences are density and content: A is sparse, isolated animal figures on an unfinished, weathered pillar with wide blank ground, while B is a densely packed figural scene with human figures, symbolic emblems and rows of sign-like marks filling nearly every surface, rendered with far finer, more controlled modelling.
